summary: Two inactive proofs show why the first-Hessian Sobolev-capacity estimate cannot be iterated for Hessian products. A logarithmic normal cutoff gives zero H1 capacity to compact pieces of smooth real codimension-two submanifolds. Two global bounded continuous omega-plurisubharmonic potentials, built from cutoff absolute real coordinates, have a positive two-factor measure charging such a set. The smoothing has a uniform lower curvature bound and the exact ddc normalization is retained. This is an obstruction to the chosen capacity estimate, not to the already proved two-factor convergence or to a different Hessian capacity.
scoped_mathematical_obligations: The chapter setting supplies n>=3 and2<=m<n, so two distinct complex coordinates and the nonnegative power omega^(m-2) exist.
A finite submanifold-chart cover reduces compact E to flat codimension-two coordinate pieces using subadditivity.
A cutoff equal to1 near the compact piece makes the radial H1 function a valid competitor on an OPEN neighborhood, not just almost everywhere on E.
The fixed smooth positive conformal Gauduchon norm is locally equivalent to the Euclidean H1 norm after flattening the submanifold.
The normal support has two-dimensional volume O(epsilon^2), bounding the L2 term and cutoff-derivative term.
The transition derivative is1/(r log(1/epsilon)); normal polar integration gives exactly1/log(1/epsilon), tending to zero.
The piecewise radial cutoff is continuous and Lipschitz for each fixed epsilon, hence a legitimate H1 function despite its corner radii.
The outer-open capacity definition and these competitors prove Cap1(E)=0 without using unproved smooth constraints on dense sets.
Compactly supported holomorphic-chart cutoffs extend both absolute-coordinate potentials continuously and boundedly by zero.
sqrt(x^2+delta^2) decreases to|x|; multiplication by the nonnegative cutoff preserves this ordering.
The singular principal Hessian term chi ddc g_delta is nonnegative; all remaining product-rule terms depend only on bounded g_delta,g_delta-prime and fixed cutoff derivatives.
The resulting lower bound -C omega is uniform in delta; one sufficiently small positive amplitude gives omega+ddc u_delta>=omega/2 for both coordinates.
The decreasing continuous limits are omega-plurisubharmonic, hence belong to the canonical bounded admissible class used by the book.
The exact convention ddc=i/(2pi) partial barpartial yields ddc g=(g-second/2) alpha with alpha=i/(4pi) dz wedge dbarz.
g-second(t)dt has total mass2 and asymptotically no mass away from0, giving the precise Dirac normalization.
The two factors involve distinct normal real variables; their product is a two-variable approximate identity, not an undefined square of the same Dirac measure.
The already proved simultaneous two-factor theorem identifies this smooth product limit with the canonical D2 in the chart.
A compact piece of{x1=x2=0} with nonempty relative interior has positive mass for the displayed tensor-product measure wedged with strictly positive omega^(n-2).
Smooth volume and both single-Hessian terms have zero mass on E because each is absolutely continuous in at least one other normal variable.
The Q2 trace expansion has exactly powers n,n-1,n-2; m cancels after the final omega^(m-2) wedge.
Positive mass on Cap1-zero E rules out a bound C Cap1(F)^b for every Borel F with any b>0, even for this one fixed positive two-factor measure.
The example uses continuous omega-psh potentials and does not contradict continuous product convergence or the active two-factor symmetry/convergence theorem.
